subject: project:gdl
value:
THE EQUIVALENT TIER'S POOL DATA IS CLEAN. The run-43 lane premise was that the camera_mode_target class - a function sitting pinned at real 0 while carrying wrong constants, invisible to every .text arbiter by construction per claim.law.SL_pool-constant-errors-are-score-invisible.20260901.v1 - would have further members among the rule-served functions. Measured at 9eb99ec5c with tools/gdl/composed_census/ce_eq_datum_audit.py: it does not. The premise is REFUTED, which per AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 5 is the deliverable.

THE AUDIT. 150 rules in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json; 145 screened; 5 unreadable. 142 VALUE-EQUAL on the RAW compiler output, 3 VALUE-DELTA, and all three are key-class artifacts rather than wrong constants, verified individually against config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt rather than assumed:
  * game/mb/mb_particle::MBPsysSetDebugNode - retail's lbl_802C9C48 (.bss, 232B), lbl_80345190 / lbl_803451BC (.sbss, 4B), lbl_803451C0 (.sbss, 1B) against our gNodeStackDirty / gNodeStackInit / gNodeStackTop / gNodeState. BSS and SBSS are zero-initialised and carry NO BYTES, so the screen cannot compare data and falls back to a key; retail's names resolve through symbols.txt to an ADDRESS key and our source's own global names do not appear in symbols.txt at all and fall to a NAME key. A:0x... can never equal N:name. Same storage, same addresses, different naming.
  * game/g3d/gcontrolpads::G3DReadControlPadStates - the same mechanism inverted: OUR side spells gPadManager, which IS in symbols.txt (.bss, 0x8029645C, 28B), so ours keys by address and the target's two corresponding relocations key elsewhere.
  * game/crt/vsprintf::vsprintf - a POINTER TABLE, keyed `P:<size>`: retail's lbl_80128508 is 360 bytes of .data and our @535 is 356. That is a genuine one-entry table-length difference and worth a look by whoever owns vsprintf, but it is a table SIZE difference, not a wrong constant.
Recorded as a law at claim.law.CE_a-bss-datum-has-no-bytes-so-the-datum-screen-keys-it-by-address-on-one-side-and-by-name-on-the-other.20260903.v1.

THE FIVE UNREADABLE PINS, named so the coverage gap is not silent: game/game/combat::DiffRate_8002951C, ::adjust_radius_8002B2D4, ::cam_orient_to_80029E8C, game/enemy/enemy::gendir_8004FBC8, game/ui/btext::FindStringMessageListSub_8001FC4C. Each is absent from BOTH objects' function lists as fndiff.parse enumerates them (all five carry an address suffix in their symbol name), so the screen has nothing to pair. 5 of 150 = 3.3% of the tier is unscreened by this audit and remains an open question.

150 RULES VERSUS 148 EQUIVALENT FUNCTIONS, RECONCILED AND BENIGN. The progress headline's 148 is the DISTINCT-FUNCTION count. Two functions carry two rule entries each - game/world/btricol::LineLineDist and game/ui/message::msgDraw - and in both cases the pair is a deliberate staged chain: an instruction_permutation-only rule followed by an instruction_permutation + copy_register_fields rule. The headline is correct and the file is not carrying stale duplicates.

THE IMAGE-WIDE HAND-OFF TABLE. The same raw-object screen run over every function of every NonMatching unit (1702 functions, build/GUNE5D/ce_image_datum.json) returns 49 VALUE-DELTA rows. Ranked by whether the disagreement is on actual datum BYTES: 32 rows carry a real byte difference and 17 are key-class artifacts of exactly the BSS mechanism above (8 pure A:, 8 mixed A:/N:, 1 pointer-table P:). The 32 real rows are the hand-off queue and cross a dozen TUs this lane does not own - notable ones being game/audio/audio::AudioStreamPlay (retail reads the string 'Audio Play Timeout' where we read 'Audio Stream bad file: %s'), game/game/combat::screen_limitation ('CONTAINER' versus 'CAM: %.2f %.2f %.2f    '), game/game/player::do_players / write_health_and_items / setup_player_display / create_player_blits / do_got_it (all five read '16_%sCOIN' where retail reads 'trbo_full_new'), game/world/camera::camera_mode_follow (retail 0.6 twice), game/game/gamemain::world_update (retail 0.1) and game/game/combat::InitCamera (retail 0.31830988614222805 = 1/pi and 180.0). None of these are in the EQUIVALENT tier and none were edited by this lane.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. This audit sees WRONG DATA, not wrong BINDINGS. cr_datum_screen's own docstring states the limit and it is real: a TRANSPOSITION preserves the multiset, so a rule that binds the right two constants to the wrong two registers reads VALUE-EQUAL here. That is precisely claim.law.CQ_copy-register-fields-can-rotate-constant-load-homes-without-their-relocations.20260903.v1 and it is the run-43 postprocessor lane's audit, not this one. A clean datum audit is necessary and not sufficient for tier soundness, and the two results must be read together.
